q: How do I estimate an air compressor's electricity and CO2 from its load and unload hours?
title: Compressor kWh from load and unload hours
short: Multiply load hours by the power drawn while loaded, add unload hours times the power drawn while unloaded, and multiply the total kWh by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh. Read the hours from the compressor controller and take both power figures from the manufacturer's data sheet or a one-off clamp meter reading.
audience: Factory maintenance and energy staff without a compressor submeter

ul: Load hours and running hours: most screw compressor controllers show both. Unload hours = running hours minus load hours.

Loaded power: input kW at your working pressure from the data sheet, or measured with a clamp meter while the machine is loading. The motor nameplate kW is shaft output, not electrical input, so do not use it as is.
Unloaded power: from the manufacturer's sheet or a clamp meter reading while the machine runs unloaded. It varies widely by machine design, so measure it rather than assume a percentage.
Reset or note the counters on a known date, so the hours match the period you report.

p: kWh = (load hours x loaded kW) + (unload hours x unloaded kW). CO2 = kWh x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for location-based Scope 2. Do this per compressor and add them; do not use one machine's figures for another.

A large share of unload hours means the compressor runs a lot without making air. That points to oversizing, poor sequencing between machines, or a pressure band set too narrow. A variable speed machine or better sequencing often cuts that unloaded energy.

A figure from hour counters and spot readings is an estimate. In your records, say so, keep the counter photos and clamp meter readings with dates, and replace it with a submeter reading when you have one. Your total Scope 2 still comes from the electricity bill; this splits it by use.

example.title: Illustrative example: a 75 kW screw compressor
lines: Controller: 6,500 running hours, 5,000 load hours, so 1,500 unload hours
Loaded input: 80 kW (clamp meter reading, assumed); unloaded input: 25 kW (assumed for this machine)
Loaded: 5,000 x 80 = 400,000 kWh; unloaded: 1,500 x 25 = 37,500 kWh
Unloaded running: 23% of hours and 8.6% of energy, spent making no air
example.note: Both power figures are illustrative assumptions; use your own measurements or the manufacturer's sheet.

senseible: Senseible applies the CEA grid factor to the kWh on your electricity bills; an equipment-level kWh you calculate this way should be kept and labelled as your estimate.
